lines.text: He turned on Athens. Then on Sparta. Then on Persia. And Athens still welcomed him home.
He was raised in the household of Pericles, the man who ran Athens.
Wealthy, gorgeous, and Socrates' favourite pupil.
He sold the city on its boldest gamble yet: the conquest of Sicily.
And Athens handed him the fleet.
But the night before it sailed, someone smashed the sacred statues of Hermes all over the city, and the blame fell on him.
Called home to stand trial, he slipped away, and sailed straight to Athens' worst enemy: Sparta.
There, he showed the Spartans exactly where to strike: save Syracuse, and build a fort outside Athens.
Then he seduced the wife of a Spartan king.
Now Sparta wanted him dead. So he ran to Persia.
At the satrap's court, he played the Greeks against each other, and dangled Persian gold in front of Athens.
Losing the war, Athens did the unthinkable. It made him general again.
He won battle after battle, and sailed home a hero.
Years later, assassins set his house on fire. He ran out, dagger in hand, and they shot him down with arrows.
His name was Alcibiades. The man who switched sides three times.
